BiblicalUsage: The word means fraudulent or tracked, crooked or followed by footprints. Jeremiah says the heart is deceitful above all things and desperately wicked; Isaiah promises the crooked shall be made straight; and Hosea calls Gilead a city tracked with blood.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the heart's deceit is the deepest problem in the Bible, deeper than any enemy outside us. The promise is that God Himself makes the crooked straight, and no one can do that work for himself.
